title: Urine-output neural model shows retrospective discrimination of severe kidney-injury events
summary: A convolutional neural network analyzed urine-output trends in 35,573 ICU patients to estimate later severe kidney-injury events under a restrictive urine-plus-creatinine definition. Patient-separated retrospective testing reported AUC 0.89, above logistic regression. Clinical prevention, calibrated alarm yield and prospective bedside benefit were not established.
ai_technology: Stacked and parallel convolutional neural networks with highway connections for urine-output time series
organization: Politecnico di Torino; National Research Council of Italy; Perugia Hospital; Terni Hospital

evidence.tested: The source pooled eICU and MIMIC-III records and separated patients across training, validation, calibration and test sets. The CNN used twelve-hour urine-output windows, with case series truncated six hours before the defined event. In the 7,080-patient test cohort, reported AUC was 0.89 versus 0.85 for logistic regression. The target required both creatinine increase and urine-output reduction; dialysis patients were excluded.
evidence.unknown: This was retrospective pooled-database evaluation, not a locked prospective clinical test. Urine output contributes to both model input and event definition; imputation and restrictive exclusions limit generalization to broader AKI. Reported likelihood ratios must not be read as positive predictive value or five true cases per six alarms. Individual-record timing, exact alarm yield and calibrated probabilities were not independently reconstructed. No reduced kidney injury, mortality or treatment benefit was demonstrated.
evidence.ai_role: The CNN learned temporal urine-output features linked to later recorded severe-AKI labels and was compared with a logistic baseline. The admitted result is specific retrospective clinical discrimination, not recovery of a single urine-output cutoff or a validated intervention.

source_review.scope: Read actual primary AKI target/eligibility, urine imputation and time truncation, patient-separated training/validation/calibration/test, CNN architecture and evaluation Methods plus clinical discrimination Results. Alarm likelihood-ratio interpretation checked and excluded from represented yield claims; individual-record timing and supplement not reconstructed. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.
